name: Happy Mondays
label: Factory Records
lede: Six lads from Salford came last in a battle of the bands at the Haçienda, made a platinum record with Bez dancing out front, then went £230,000 over budget in Barbados the year Factory went under.

eras.title: Last place at the Haçienda
eras.text: Two brothers from Little Hulton, three mates and, by Pride of Manchester's account, a lot of borrowed-without-asking gear. They lost a battle of the bands at Factory's own club and got a Factory deal anyway, then added a sixth member whose instrument was dancing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Pride of Manchester · Classic Pop
years.h: The Ryder brothers start a band in Salford
years.p: [[Shaun Ryder|cb72e132-66c1-44c2-986f-eed70d97d29a]] sings, his younger brother [[Paul Ryder|8bead127-8711-4baf-a8e6-790885f58bdc]] plays bass, with [[Mark Day|3c052e7b-5451-4545-896b-be4cc92ef754]] on guitar, [[Paul Davis|a2b4fe08-3b6c-4e9b-bf26-602ab626f98a]] on keyboards and [[Gary Whelan|ddd000cc-9616-43b3-9686-226f024ec103]] on drums. It takes five years to get a record out.
years.xp: Pride of Manchester's history says the band "admitted to having stolen most of their equipment." It dates the start to 1984, when Shaun was 22 and Paul 20; Wikipedia and Classic Pop say 1980.

years.src: Pride of Manchester · Wikipedia: Happy Mondays
years.h: Happy Mondays come last in Mike Pickering's battle of the bands
years.p: The contest is at the Haçienda. Tony Wilson signs them to Factory anyway, after Phil Saxe, who sold clothes at the Arndale, gets their demo to Pickering and on to Wilson.

years.h: Bez joins on maracas and dancing
years.p: Shaun talks his friend Mark "Bez" Berry into dancing on the Haçienda stage. Pride of Manchester: "The crowd loved him." He stays as the sixth member.

years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Pride of Manchester
years.h: The Forty Five EP, also known as Delightful
years.p: The first Happy Mondays record, on Factory. It doesn't chart.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bez · Pride of Manchester · Toppermost
years.h: Bez cuts his head open on stage and comes back with the shakers
years.p: At a Haçienda gig he falls off the stage. His dancing has already given the band a single, "Freaky Dancin'."
years.xp: Bez's own account of the fix: "I got some lead guitarist Moose's acid, dripped it in the cut and ran back out with me shakers."

eras.title: Tangerines, Driffield and a writ from Michael Jackson
eras.text: A Velvet Underground founder produced the first album and a Joy Division producer the second. By the end of 1989 the band were on Top of the Pops next to the Stone Roses and Manchester had a new nickname.

years.h: John Cale produces the debut, and eats a lot of tangerines
years.p: Two weeks at the Fire House in London in December 1986, for £6,000. Halfway through, they scrap everything and start again.
years.xp:
[[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] picked the studio because he'd been in a band with its owner, Dave Young. Young said the band "did not seem to know what they were playing much of the time"; Ryder wrote lyrics on scraps of paper and threw them away. Cale was staying sober and eating tangerines, and the band complained that was all he did.

The title came from a friend, Little Mini, who walked in and said most of it in one breath. It sold about 3,500 copies in six months. "I thought that meant loads of money would come in, but it meant absolutely fuck all," Ryder said of the good reviews.
play: Squirrel and G-Man Twenty Four Hour Party People Plastic Face Carnt Smile (White Out)

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel and G-Man · Pride of Manchester
years.h: "Desmond" draws a writ from Michael Jackson's lawyers
years.p: The song borrowed the tune of the Beatles' "Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da," whose publisher Jackson owned. After 3,000 copies, the album comes back with "24 Hour Party People" in its place.

years.h: Martin Hannett makes Bummed on a farm in Driffield
years.p: Recorded mostly live at the Slaughterhouse in August, far from Manchester's ecstasy supply. NME gives it 9 out of 10; it peaks at No. 59.
years.xp: [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]] had the band play songs over and over for hours, and ran Paul Ryder's bass through digital filters and pedals. Central Station Design painted Shaun's face for the cover; a Penthouse image on the inner sleeve got the record refused by some shops and confiscated by Japanese customs.

years.cap: Happy Mondays at the Free Trade Hall, Manchester, November 1989
years.h: Paul Oakenfold and Vince Clarke remix "Wrote for Luck"
years.p: "W.F.L." puts the band into house clubs. The NME names it best dance record.

years.src: Toppermost · Classic Pop · Pride of Manchester
yt: Hallelujah, Top of the Pops, November 1989
years.h: Happy Mondays and the Stone Roses share one Top of the Pops
years.p: The Mondays play "Hallelujah" from the Madchester Rave On EP, with Kirsty MacColl on the single. The EP reaches No. 19.

years.h: Rowetta thought "give us a nosh" meant cooking
years.p: [[Rowetta|2fbc1566-4df2-4f54-99aa-d98a43a6c600]] saw the band on Granada's The Other Side of Midnight and came in on backing vocals, first as a guest.
years.xp: "I always wanted to be in a punk band," she told Classic Pop, but her voice suited what the Mondays had become. Her line about Shaun's invitation: "I thought he wanted me to cook when he said 'give us a nosh.'"

eras.title: Platinum from the Oakwood Apartments
eras.text: Two Top 5 singles, a Glastonbury headline slot and a platinum record made in Los Angeles with the families along. For a year nobody in British music was bigger.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches · DJ Mag
years.h: "Step On" was meant for an Elektra birthday album
years.p: The John Kongos cover was cut for Rubáiyát, Elektra's 40th anniversary compilation. The band gave Elektra a different Kongos song and kept this one. It reaches No. 5.

years.h: The Mondays headline the Friday night at Glastonbury
years.p: Same summer, same band that came last at the Haçienda five years before.

years.src: DJ Mag · Wikipedia: Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches
years.h: Oakenfold produces the band one at a time in Los Angeles
years.p: [[Paul Oakenfold|7bf1f441-ccf1-4258-9797-07c8d16eb44c]] and Steve Osborne record at Capitol Studios, with the band and their families at the Oakwood Apartments.
years.xp: "We recorded them individually... We approached it like a DJ makes music," Oakenfold told DJ Mag. Session player Tony Castro added percussion to "Loose Fit" and "Bob's Yer Uncle"; Wikipedia's account puts that down to Bez's "lacklustre skills as a percussionist."

years.src: Wikipedia: Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches · Wikipedia: Happy Mondays
years.h: Pills 'n' Thrills and Bellyaches goes platinum
years.p: No. 4 in the UK, 28 weeks on the chart. "Kinky Afro" had already hit No. 5.
years.xp: Central Station Design built the sleeve from American candy wrappers and cartoon lettering; Factory flew the designers to Los Angeles to collect material. The BPI certified it platinum in March 1991. Wikipedia gives UK sales as 400,000; the band's own article says over 350,000.

years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Wikipedia: Shaun Ryder
years.h: Paul McCartney tells the NME the Mondays remind him of the Beatles
years.p: McCartney had seen the band on TV.

years.h: Rock in Rio, then lunch with Ronnie Biggs
years.p: The band plays the Maracanã at Rock in Rio 2 and meets the Great Train Robber with journalist Piers Morgan.

years.cap: Ticket for Happy Mondays at Elland Road, Leeds, 1991
years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Discogs: Baby Big Head
years.h: Thirty thousand at Elland Road, Leeds
years.p: Wikipedia calls it the Mondays' own Spike Island. Factory releases the recording as Baby Big Head, sold as an official bootleg, before the Live album.

eras.title: Barbados
eras.text: Factory sent the band to Eddy Grant's studio to make the follow-up with two Talking Heads. It ran more than double its budget, the label went under that November, and a rescue deal with EMI ended at one meeting.

years.h: Bez makes homophobic comments in an NME interview
years.p: DJ Mag calls them horribly homophobic. The interview was to promote the single "Judge Fudge."

q: Fleetwood Mac did more fucking drugs than we did.
years.h: Yes Please! is recorded in Barbados, and barely
years.p: Chris Frantz and Tina Weymouth produce at Eddy Grant's Blue Wave Studio. Shaun is smoking crack and can't sing; the vocals get done in Surrey in May. Ryder has pushed back on the legend since.
years.xp:
Classic Pop says Ryder's methadone broke at the airport on the way out, and crack was easy to find on the island. Wikipedia's account has him spending 20 hours a day in the toilet smoking it, which gave him a throat infection. Bez broke his arm three times: in a car crash, in a boat accident, and when his girlfriend sat on it. In March Ryder went into the Charter Clinic in Chelsea for six weeks.

"The first day we got there I was in tears, just thinking 'this is mental,'" Mark Day told Classic Pop.

years.h: Yes Please! stalls at No. 14
years.p: "Stinkin' Thinkin'" goes to No. 1 on Billboard's dance chart in America and No. 31 at home. Select called the album "so disappointing"; Q said they'd pulled it off again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yes Please! · Wikipedia: Happy Mondays
years.h: Factory Records goes into administration
years.p: The label that signed the Mondays after a last-place finish is gone. Yes Please! had cost it £380,000.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yes Please! · Pride of Manchester
years.h: Shaun walks out of the EMI meeting to buy "Kentucky"
years.p: EMI's Clive Black is there to sign the band. Ryder announces he's leaving to buy heroin, using the slang, and Black ends talks. The band splits.

eras.title: Black Grape, then the boys are back
eras.text: Shaun and Bez had a No. 1 album with a new band before the Mondays name came back. The first reunion lasted two years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shaun Ryder · Wikipedia: Happy Mondays
years.h: Black Grape's debut tops the UK album chart
years.p: Shaun and Bez's new band, with guitarist Wags and rapper Kermit, goes to No. 1 with It's Great When You're Straight... Yeah.

years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Wikipedia: Paul Ryder
years.h: The Mondays re-form and cover "The Boys Are Back in Town"
years.p: Without Day and Davis, they sell out Manchester's 20,000-capacity arena and take the Thin Lizzy cover to No. 24, then support [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]]. Paul Ryder's exit in 2001 ends it.
years.xp: Both brothers had battled heroin addiction through the 1990s, Wikipedia notes, and it caused a falling-out between them.

years.h: 24 Hour Party People puts the Mondays on screen
years.p: In the Factory film, Paul Ryder turns up as a gangster and Rowetta plays herself.

eras.title: Shaun's Mondays
eras.text: Shaun, Bez and Whelan brought the name back with hired hands. Paul had sworn never to play with his brother again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Happy Mondays · Wikipedia: Paul Ryder
years.h: A new Mondays, without Paul Ryder
years.p: Shaun hires Kav Sandhu and Jonn Dunn on guitars and Mikey Shine on bass. Paul starts his own band, Big Arm.

years.h: Bez wins Celebrity Big Brother; Shaun sings on a No. 1
years.p: Ryder's turn on [[Gorillaz|e21857d5-3256-4547-afb3-4b6ded592596]]' "Dare" gives that band its only UK No. 1.

years.h: First album in 15 years, and Tony Wilson gives it a Factory number
years.p: Sunny Levine and Howie B produce. It comes out on Big Brother Records.

years.h: Coachella, before Rage Against the Machine, minus Bez
years.p: Bez misses the show over passport trouble.

eras.title: Without the madness
eras.text: Twenty years after the split, the original six and Rowetta made it up. They've toured on and off since, through Paul Ryder's death in 2022.

years.cap: Bez on stage with Happy Mondays
years.h: Shaun announces the original line-up is back, on Xfm
years.p: Both Ryders, Day, Davis, Whelan, Bez and Rowetta. The May UK tour mostly sells out and adds a Brixton date.
years.xp: Ryder said amends had been made and friendships reinstated, and that it was "just like the old days, but without the madness." Day had spent 17 years away teaching music in schools, Classic Pop reports.

years.h: Twenty-five years of Bummed, without Paul Davis
years.p: The keyboardist leaves after a year back. The band tours the album's anniversary, and Bummed wins Q's Classic Album award.

years.h: "Ooo La La to Panama," recorded with the Emberá
years.p: The band travels to Panama and records with the Emberá people, billed as the original line-up's first recording since 1992.

years.h: Paul Ryder dies at 58, the day of a Sunderland show
years.p: He had flown in from Los Angeles and complained of headaches. His mother found him; the coroner gave ischaemic heart disease and diabetes as the causes.

years.cap: Happy Mondays at O2 City Hall, Newcastle
years.h: Pills 'n' Thrills at 35 gets a tour
years.p: After a March 2024 tour with Inspiral Carpets, Shaun had talked of years off. The band announces UK and Irish dates for spring 2026, with the Farm and Northside opening.

sources.title: DJ Mag: How Pills 'N' Thrills became the pinnacle of the Madchester sound
